flags.note: The passage never states the narrator's gender, but this item (and R065-04, -05, -08, -10) refers to the narrator as 'her/she'. It does not affect any key. Consider adding a gender cue to the passage or using neutral wording.

R065-01.notes: A: she chooses the linkage replacement (p4), then calls back for 'Cleaning only' (p6). B: she never learns repair or opens a business. C: her mother wanted to give it away, but there is no argument and the narrator keeps it. D: the reverse is true; the same lift shows it is the same machine.

R065-02.notes: C: 'it will never stick again.' A: the second option was three times the price of the first. B: color is never mentioned. D: nothing is said about time.

R065-03.notes: B: the bar 'hung there a beat too long... unless I waited', so typing keeps stopping. A is the intended trap: the image sounds leisurely, but the context is frustration. C: the problem is delay, not speed. D: she can type, just slowly ('The machine worked, mostly').

R065-04.notes: D: 'respectful' toward the inherited machine and Vesna, and the ending reframes this belief. A: there is no sign that Pellerin would be offended. B: cleaning is never said to cause damage. C: the mother wanted to give the machine away and is not involved in the repair.

R065-05.notes: A: 'For comparison... Afterward,' and she lays his line beside Vesna's letters. B: there is no doubt about payment. C: the line is legible and shows the lift. D: he types 'slowly'.

R065-06.notes: C: 'did not sound surprised', and his comparison sample suggests he anticipated her change of mind. A: there is no disappointment, and he says 'You'll learn the rhythm.' B: he says the e will 'still stick a little', which is a partial fix, not 'not at all'. D: there is no evidence of work already begun.

R065-07.notes: B: he waits for each sticking type bar to fall back to its resting position before typing the next letter. A and C are literal senses of the phrase that do not fit a machine part. D: the problem is the bar lingering, not force, and he types slowly and gently.

R065-08.notes: D: 'help me keep someone... nearly paid him to erase her'. The lifted e is Vesna's trace in the machine. B: the existing letters would stay readable. C: the carbons are paper and would not be harmed by the repair. A: there is no suggestion of insulting him.

R065-09.notes: B: 'carbon copies, one for every letter she had sent.' A: they are Vesna's own letters, and the narrator had never read them. C: the letters were sent, not unmailed drafts. D: they were in the box, not left by Pellerin.

R065-10.notes: C: 'asked for it before I knew why... not sure I could explain myself.' A: she shows no regret. B: the typewriter looks 'faintly ridiculous' beside the laptop and does not match it. D: she is not indifferent, and she does type on it.
